winner_in_my_two: STUDY MARKED: WON — 7/4F (banked 13/8), by 7.5L 'easily, eased final 110yds'; paper level stake +1.75
error: WINNER: Aegean Prince (Appleby/Buick, Godolphin, top weight 9-12, 320 days off) — took a keen hold, prominent, led over 2f out, went clear, eased down; In The Breeze 12/1 2nd (my third, the Blanco read: 'the soft-ground 5L winner'), Pole Star 14/1 3rd (first-time cheekpieces), Stressfree 13/2 4th (the named danger, 'in rear, modest fourth'), Finalise 100/30 7th (the second danger, led after 3f, weakened)
column8: ERROR (none on the verdict): the sheet's decisive line — 'unexposed, the TELL present (top yard, number-one rider, the owner, a big day), trip and soft ground proven at 3/5 in France' — was the reason he won, and the discipline held: one line per principal, the tell weighed as the fact it is; the weak point was the second danger (Finalise, the keen front-runner who was always going to be caught on heavy) over In The Breeze, whom my own Blanco read had as the proven soft-ground stayer
column9: CALIBRATION: (1) THE TWO LESSONS OF THE DAY MET HEAD-ON AND THE TELL WON: the Past Winners (his paste, nine runnings 2017-2025) say no winner above 9-7, most 8-10 to 9-5 — and the top weight at 9-12 won by 7.5L; the Kempton lesson (class at level weights) and the Haydock 1:55 lesson (the unexposed floor with the tell is unbounded) OUTRANKED the race's weight DNA: a Listed-class Godolphin horse in a Class 2 handicap off 99 is not a handicapper carrying 9-12, he is a class horse slumming — the DNA is a PRIOR about ordinary handicappers, and the tell says this one is not ordinary. The order of the facts, as the day taught it: class/the tell FIRST, then the race's DNA, then the surface/course lines. (2) FOUR NON-RUNNERS ON THE GROUND (Dancing In Paris, Mountain Road, Synergism, Valedictory 'unsuitable ground'): the ground took out a third of the field and left a race the class horse could dominate — the non-runners are a fact about the race's shape and the sheet read them only as 'NR'. (3) THE 320-DAY ABSENCE was a caution stated and did not bite — Appleby's horses win fresh; the yard is the receipt (no rule carved: n=1). (4) STRESSFREE, THE EXPOSED FIGURE HORSE (RP top-rated 107, the Ebor line), 4th beaten 13L: the volume-over-weight fault would have picked him — the figure horse in a race the tell horse dominated; the day's lesson held in the one race I applied it before the verdict. (5) Sittings today: 1 from 4 settled (Rocket Boy 2nd, Archers Bay 3rd, Gethin 2nd, Aegean Prince WON); the winner came the first time the tell was weighed as a fact BEFORE the verdict.
